title: EM-Optimized Cryostat Sectioning (EMOCS) of Tissues for Large-Scale Detection of Antigens by Immunofluorescence and Immunoelectron Microscopy
content:
Abstract
Cryosections are widely used in biomedical research because they preserve enzymatic activity, antigenicity, and histomorphology, making them suitable for immunohistochemical and immunofluorescence light microscopy. However, achieving adequate ultrastructural quality for immunoelectron microscopy (IEM) across large imaging fields remains challenging. Here, we introduce electron microscopy (EM)-optimized cryostat sectioning (EMOCS), an improved method that combines freeze protection using high sucrose concentrations, similar to the Tokuyasu method, with measures to minimize drying and compression artifacts and optimize short-term storage. EMOCS routinely yields sections with excellent histologic and ultrastructural preservation across diverse tissues. The method supports antigen detection via immunofluorescence microscopy (IFM), pre-embedding IEM with fluoronanogold labeling, and immunoenzymatic silver metallography, thereby substantially expanding the utility of cryostat sections for large-scale IFM and IEM.
